title: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self
line: Jung wrote Aion in 1951 about the age of the Fishes and the figure that stands at its centre. It starts with the parts of the psyche you can meet, and ends with the self. Walk it chapter by chapter, in his order.

chapters.title: Foreword
chapters.line: What the book is about: the Christian aeon read through its symbols of the self, and the turn it carries inside it.

quotes.text: My investigation seeks, with the help of Christian, Gnostic, and alchemical symbols of the self, to throw light on the change of psychic situation within the "Christian aeon."

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

quotes.text: It is therefore only natural that my reflections should gravitate mainly round the symbol of the Fishes, for the Pisces aeon is the synchronistic concomitant of two thousand years of Christian development.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

chapters.title: The Ego
chapters.line: He starts with the one part everyone knows: the ego, the centre of what we are aware of.

quotes.text: We understand the ego as the complex factor to which all conscious contents are related.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

quotes.text: It forms, as it were, the centre of the field of consciousness; and, in so far as this comprises the empirical personality, the ego is the subject of all personal acts of consciousness.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

chapters.title: The Shadow
chapters.line: The first figure the ego meets is its own shadow, and meeting it is a moral task.

quotes.text: The only exceptions to this rule are those rather rare cases where the positive qualities of the personality are repressed, and the ego in consequence plays an essentially negative or unfavourable role. >4 The shadow is a moral problem that challenges the whole ego-personality, for no one can become conscious of the shadow without considerable moral effort.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

quotes.text: Hence one meets with projections, one does not make them.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

chapters.title: The Syzygy: Anima and Animus
chapters.line: Behind the shadow stand the contrasexual figures, the anima and the animus, a pair.

quotes.text: What, then, is this projection-making factor? The East calls it the "Spinning Woman"

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

quotes.text: The animus corresponds to the paternal Logos just as the anima corresponds to the maternal Eros.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

chapters.title: The Self
chapters.line: Then the whole: the self, whose images cannot be told apart from images of God.

quotes.text: Unity and totality stand at the highest point on the scale of objective values because their symbols can no longer be distinguished from the imago Dei.

chapters.line: For the Christian aeon, the self had a face: Christ, with Antichrist as his shadow.

quotes.text: Christ exemplifies the archetype of the self.

chapters.title: The Historical Significance of the Fish
chapters.line: The shepherd and the fish meet where one aeon hands over to the next.

quotes.text: Shepherd, ram, and lamb symbolism coincides with the expiring aeon of Aries.

chapters.title: The Fish in Alchemy
chapters.line: In alchemy the fish turns into the arcane substance, and it still rises in dreams today.

quotes.text: Whether he knew that the fish was a symbol for the arcane substance and the lapis is perhaps questionable, but it is more than likely that he had read the classics of alchemy.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

quotes.text: In conclusion, I would like to give a concrete example of the way the symbol of the fish springs out of the unconscious autochthonously.

chapters.title: The Alchemical Interpretation of the Fish
chapters.line: The pull that once came from the fish passes to a magnet the alchemist holds.

quotes.text: I mention this seemingly unimportant feature because, as we shall see, in the alchemical view the attraction no longer proceeds from the fish but from a magnet which man possesses and which exerts the attraction that was once the mysterious property of the fish.

chapters.title: Background to the Psychology of Christian Alchemical Symbolism
chapters.line: Alchemy as the mother of an epoch, born of the Gnostic systems and lost to the age of science.

quotes.text: "Mater Alchimia" could serve as the name of a whole epoch.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

quotes.text: It owes its real beginnings to the Gnostic systems, which Hippolytus rightly regarded as philosophic, and which, with the help of Greek philosophy and the mythologies of the Near and Middle East, together with Christian dogmatics and Jewish cabalism, made extremely interesting attempts, from the modern point of view, to synthetize a unitary vision of the world in which the physical and the mystical aspects played equal parts.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

chapters.title: Gnostic Symbols of the Self
chapters.line: What the aeon slowly worked out was already pictured by the Gnostics at its start.

quotes.text: Since all cognition is akin to recognition, it should not come as a surprise to find that what I have described as a gradual process of development had already been anticipated, and more or less prefigured, at the beginning of our era.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

chapters.title: The Structure and Dynamics of the Self
chapters.line: He gathers the images into one picture: the self as a structure of fours that keeps transforming.

quotes.text: The examples given in the previous chapter should be sufficient to describe the progressive assimilation and amplification of the archetype that underlies ego-consciousness.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

quotes.text: From various hints dropped by Hippolytus, it is clear beyond a doubt that many of the Gnostics were nothing other than psychologists.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

chapters.title: Conclusion
chapters.line: The book's own summary: shadow, syzygy, and the self they lead to.

quotes.text: I have tried, in this book, to elucidate and amplify the various aspects of the archetype which it is most important for modern man to understand—namely, the archetype of the self.
